# `Q-9-15` — Invalid CSL Version

> The `version` attribute on `<cs:style>` is not a recognized
> CSL version.

## What this means

Every CSL style declares the CSL specification version it
targets: `<cs:style version="1.0" ...>`. The version is used to
pick the right validation rules and the right rendering
semantics. This error fires when the version attribute is
present but does not parse as a valid CSL version — usually
because it is not in the `major.minor` format the parser
expects.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **A typo** — `version="0.1"` instead of `version="1.0"`.
- **A missing or extra character** that breaks the
  `major.minor` shape.
- **A vendor-specific version string** added by another tool
  that the parser does not recognize.

## How to fix

Set `version` to a valid CSL version string in `major.minor`
form — `"1.0"` for the current CSL 1.0 specification, or
`"1.1"` for the in-progress 1.1 work. Match the version that
the rest of the style was authored against.

## Related

- `Q-9-16` — invalid root element: a related top-level CSL
  shape error, where `<cs:style>` itself is missing.
- `Q-9-7` — the `version` attribute is missing entirely.
